entry_audit.question: Should related messages be combined using completion and timeout rules?
Should a local proxy mediate a client's network capabilities, rather than embedding connectivity logic in the client or centralizing it remotely?
Should a translation layer protect the domain model from a legacy or external model with different semantics?
Should an in-memory composition layer assemble a response from several service owners, rather than forcing one owner to duplicate all data?
Should external clients enter through a managed gateway that owns routing, authentication and cross-cutting edge policy?
Should a client submit work and later fetch a result, rather than hold one synchronous request open?
Should security-relevant actions be recorded in an append-only, attributable log?
Should capacity be adjusted automatically from observed or predicted demand?
Should each client population get a tailored server contract, rather than share one general-purpose API?
Should recovery rely on base backups plus point-in-time WAL/log replay?
Should traffic switch between two complete environments rather than replace in place?
Should an internal abstraction seam allow old/new implementations to coexist in one deployable?
Should concurrency or resources for one dependency be isolated from the rest of the workload?
Should the application populate the cache after a miss instead of routing every read through the cache layer?
Should cached entries be removed or refreshed when the authoritative value changes?
Should concurrent misses be coordinated so they do not all hit the source at once?
Should a new version receive a small traffic share before full promotion?
Should interapplication messages use a shared canonical model rather than point-to-point translations?
Should operations that are causally related preserve their order without requiring a total order?
Should content be cached at the edge close to clients rather than only at the origin?
Should the system be partitioned into cells with bounded blast radius and independent operation?
Should database changes be captured as a replayable stream instead of dual-written by the application?
Should calls to a failing dependency be rejected early until it recovers?
Should large or sensitive payloads be stored separately and referenced by a claim check?
Should dependencies point inward toward domain policies, with frameworks and delivery mechanisms at the outside?
Should the caller own service lookup and backend selection, rather than delegating both to an intermediary?
Should command and query models be separated so reads and writes can evolve independently?
Should a command service keep a local read replica of remote facts to decide without synchronous calls?
Should a failed saga step be undone by an explicit business compensation rather than a rollback?
Should multiple consumers share one queue to scale processing and smooth bursts?
Should replicas agree on an ordered log despite failures and partitions?
Should keys and nodes share a hash ring so membership changes move only a fraction of data?
Should routing be decided from message content rather than a fixed destination?
Should the final authority switch be gated by explicit go/no-go evidence and a no-return contract?
Should related messages carry an explicit identifier so replies and follow-ups can be matched?
Should a read model be projected asynchronously from an authoritative write model?
Should new code receive real or shadow traffic before it is authoritative?
Should each service own its authoritative data and expose only a contract, rather than share one database across services?
Should messages that cannot be processed be isolated in a dead-letter channel?
Should the caller’s remaining time budget be passed through downstream calls?
Should independent deployment units be replicated as stamps for scale, isolation or locality?
Should cached data live in a shared distributed tier rather than only inside each process?
Should a shared lock prevent concurrent access to one resource across processes?
Should requests carry a trace context so spans across services can be correlated?
Should a durable orchestration engine own multi-step progress, timers and recovery?
Should models and ownership be separated by bounded context rather than forced into one shared enterprise model?
Should a meaningful state change be published as an event that other owners can react to?
Should a subscriber retain messages across temporary disconnects?
Should a consumer be invoked by message arrival rather than polling on a schedule?
Should authoritative state be derived from an ordered event history rather than stored as current rows?
Should a schema change be rolled out in expand, migrate and contract stages?
Should a schema change be deployed in expand, migrate and contract stages?
Should traffic move to a standby and later return to the original authority?
Should a failed primary path return a defined degraded result?
Should activation be decoupled from deployment through a runtime toggle?
Should identity be asserted by a trusted issuer and accepted across services, rather than locally re-authenticated?
Should every write carry an epoch/token so the destination rejects a stale owner?
Should a narrow gatekeeper validate and shape requests before they reach a sensitive backend, rather than exposing the backend directly?
Should a gateway aggregate several downstream responses into one client-facing result, rather than making the client orchestrate every call?
Should reusable cross-cutting functions be moved to a gateway without moving domain authority there?
Should a gateway route requests to the responsible backend using an explicit contract rather than exposing every backend address to clients?
Should identical nodes be deployed across regions behind a global routing layer?
Should desired state be versioned and reconciled automatically from a Git source?
Should non-essential capabilities be reduced to protect essential work under stress?
Should an external monitor distinguish liveness, readiness and startup health?
Should the runtime distinguish process liveness, traffic readiness and startup completion?
Should a duplicate request be issued after a latency threshold to reduce tail latency?
Should domain logic be isolated from input/output technology through explicit ports and adapters?
Should capacity be added by running more instances rather than a larger instance?
Should a client-supplied key let the server recognize retries of one logical request?
Should the receiver detect duplicate deliveries and avoid duplicate effects?
Should infrastructure be replaced rather than mutated in place?
Should a separate lookup table maintain a secondary access path?
Should responsibilities be grouped into layers with an enforced dependency direction, rather than organized around ports or independently deployed services?
Should one node be chosen to coordinate work while others stand by?
Should one leader accept writes while followers replicate and serve reads?
Should ownership expire after a bounded lease rather than remain until explicit release?
Should each identity and workload hold only the permissions needed for its current task?
Should requests be distributed across equivalent backends by a resolver or proxy?
Should the system reject some work to preserve useful throughput under overload?
Should a query result be stored and refreshed explicitly rather than recomputed per request?
Should a broker mediate routing and delivery between producers and consumers, possibly bridging protocols?
Should messages be removed when they do not meet explicit criteria?
Should bounded business capabilities be independently deployable services with explicit distributed costs, rather than one deployable with module boundaries?
Should a bounded capability remain one deployable with enforced module boundaries, rather than split into independently deployed services?
Should more than one node accept writes for the same data?
Should data be cached in more than one tier with different latency and freshness?
Should tenants be isolated in compute, data, identity and network layers rather than share one trusted pool?
Should failures or empty results be cached like successful responses?
Should data be backfilled while the system continues serving reads and writes?
Should old and new implementations process the same work concurrently for comparison?
Should a large table or stream be divided into partitions for pruning, retention or parallelism?
Should processing be composed as independent stages connected by channels?
Should each message be consumed by exactly one worker, rather than broadcast to all subscribers?
Should different data responsibilities use different stores while one authoritative boundary owns consistency?
Should queued work be ordered by business priority rather than arrival?
Should a durable coordinator or a routing-slip itinerary own a multi-step message flow and its recovery?
Should one event reach all interested subscribers without the publisher knowing their count?
Should work be buffered in a queue so producers and consumers can run at different rates?
Should reads and writes require intersecting majorities to guarantee consistency?
Should decisions require a majority of replicas rather than one node?
Should each client or tenant have an enforced request budget?
Should access be decided by roles or attributes rather than ad hoc checks?
Should read-only replicas serve queries to offload the writer?
Should the cache layer load missing data on behalf of the application?
Should a request and its response travel as correlated messages rather than one synchronous call?
Should out-of-order messages be buffered and released in an acceptable order?
Should a failed call be retried after increasing delays?
Should retry delays include randomness to avoid synchronized retries?
Should a reverse proxy terminate client connections and forward requests to backends, rather than exposing backends directly?
Should instances be replaced incrementally while traffic continues?
Should a multi-service business process be coordinated through local transactions and compensations?
Should saga participants react to events without a central coordinator?
Should a central coordinator drive saga steps and compensations?
Should one request be broadcast to several recipients and their responses combined?
Should a service reduce synchronous dependencies by owning or duplicating the data and behavior it needs, rather than calling other services on every request?
Should a proxy or load balancer own service lookup and backend selection for the caller?
Should callers resolve backend instances through a discovery mechanism rather than static addresses?
Should independently governed services and contracts be composed across organizational boundaries, rather than designed as one application or one microservice estate?
Should one client session preserve selected read/write observations across replicas?
Should data be split across shards by a partition key to scale beyond one node?
Should each tenant be assigned a random subset of shards to reduce overlapping blast radius?
Should auxiliary runtime behavior run in a colocated process/container beside the main workload, rather than inside it or in a separate remote service?
Should duplicate in-flight requests for the same key share one source call?
Should service health be governed by user-visible indicators, objectives and an explicit error budget?
Should a composite message be divided into independently processed parts?
Should a stale response be served while a refresh runs in the background?
Should static content be served from a dedicated store or edge rather than the application origin?
Should a legacy capability be replaced incrementally behind a routing seam rather than by a rewrite?
Should logs be emitted as structured events with stable fields rather than free text?
Should probes exercise user-visible behavior from outside the service rather than rely only on internal metrics?
Should tenants receive isolated compute/data/networking quotas rather than share one unbounded pool?
Should request rate be limited to protect a dependency or budget?
Should each call have a bounded wait before it is treated as failed?
Should message identity and consumer effect be recorded atomically to suppress duplicates?
Should publication intent be stored in the same local transaction as the state change?
Should entries expire after a bounded time even without an explicit invalidation?
Should a distributed transaction use a prepare/commit protocol across resource managers?
Should a client receive a scoped, time-limited credential for direct resource access?
Should capacity be added by increasing CPU/memory/IO on one instance?
Should workloads authenticate each other with cryptographic identities rather than network location?
Should writes bypass the cache and invalidate or refresh it later?
Should writes land in the cache first and reach the store asynchronously?
Should every write update the cache and the authoritative store together?
Should every access be authenticated and authorized at the resource, rather than trusted because it is inside a network?
